 Wednesday, November 18, 2026
 Nov 18 
 Written by Shawn Mannon 
 POPLAR BLUFF JUNIOR HIGH STUDENTS TO WALK TODAY IN HONOR OF RUBY BRIDGES WALK TO SCHOOL DAY 
 Poplar Bluff Junior High School students will be out walking today for Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day. 
 Ruby Bridges was the first black child to attend an all-white school in the South. On November 14, 1960, U.S. marshals escorted Ruby and her mother as they walked to her first day at William Frantz Elementary School.
 School officials say that a Multicultural World Class will honor Ruby’s courage this afternoon by walking from the Junior High to River Radio and back. 
 HUNTERS ENCOURAGED TO SHARE THEIR HARVEST WITH FAMILIES IN NEED 
 Hunters across the state of Missouri are being asked to share their harvest this fall to help feed families in need. 
 The Missouri Department of Conservation Share the Harvest program provides food to the hungry through deer meat donated by hunters. 
 Hunters can choose to give part or all of any deer they harvest. They simply bring their deer to an approved meat processor to process the venison, usually into ground meat, where it is then packaged for distribution. 
 Share the Harvest is a statewide partnership between MDC, the Conservation Federation of Missouri, cooperating meat processors, and hunters. 
 For more details on the Share the Harvest program and a list of processors participating, visit mdc.mo.gov/share.
 WILD TURKEY WEDNESDAY IN DONIPHAN TO RAISE MONEY FOR CHRISTMAS MEAL 
 A special event has been scheduled for next week in Ripley County to raise money for Christmas meals. 
 Wild Turkey Wednesday will be held at 6 pm on November 25th at 1808 Public House in Doniphan. Admission is free. 
 There will also be an auction for baked goods, gift cards, and merchandise and other items from businesses throughout Butler and Ripley Counties. 
 50 percent of the auction proceeds will benefit the VFW and Doniphan Gospel Rescue Mission to help fund the Christmas meal they provide for local veterans and those less fortunate.
 THREE RIVERS COLLEGE COMMUNITY CHOIR TO HOST CHOIR CONCERT IN DECEMBER 
 The Three Rivers College Community Choir will be hosting a concert in December. 
 Christmas at the Tinnin has been scheduled for 7 pm on Saturday, December 5th and 2 pm on December 6th at the Tinnin Fine Arts Center in Poplar Bluff. 
 Tickets are $20 and are available online at tinnin.ticketleap.com . Tickets will be sold at the door, if any remain.
 More information is available at trcc.edu/events. 
 ROAD PROJECT UNDERWAY ON ROUTE H IN STODDARD COUNTY 
 Route H in Stoddard County will be reduced this week as Missouri Department of Transportation crews perform shoulder work. 
 The section of roadway being reduced is located from Route ZZ to County Road 637 near Dexter. 
 Weather permitting, work will take place from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. today and tomorrow. 
 ROADSIDE WORK SCHEDULED FOR THIS WEEK IN PEMISCOT COUNTY 
 Route YY in Pemiscot County will be reduced to one lane with a 12-foot width restriction this week as construction crews perform roadside work.   
 According to the Missouri Department of Transportation, the section of roadway being reduced is located near County Road 209. 
 Weather permitting, work will be performed today through Friday, from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily. 
 Shawn Mannon
